thought: Polio left her leg permanently impaired. Her first husband stripped her and threw her and her two daughters out of their home. She didn't find her sport until she was 34.
support: Sharmila Dhankar, born in Chhithroli village, Haryana, contracted polio at age 2, leaving her with a permanently impaired left leg. Married at 19, she endured years of domestic abuse until her first husband threw her and her two daughters out of their home, leaving her suicidal and depressed. She rebuilt her life raising her daughters alone, and only discovered para athletics in 2020, at around age 34. Within a year she became national champion in women's shot put F57. After a heartbreaking fourth-place finish at the Birmingham 2022 Commonwealth Games and the loss of her father a year before Glasgow 2026 - with her mother Santosh selling part of the family's farmland to help fund her training - Dhankar threw a season-best 9.81m at the 2026 Commonwealth Games in Glasgow to win gold, at age 40. It was India's first-ever Commonwealth Games gold in para-athletics, ending a 20-year medal wait for India in the discipline.
